title: The plan card — three ways to lay it out

steps.path: A plan the assistant has proposed, waiting for your approval
steps.headline: Which of these lets you see what the plan will do without reading it?
steps.notice: All three show the same plan: three helpers read the changed files at once, one checks their notes, one writes the ranked list. Every row is the app's own row — click one and it opens in place, the way a Settings section does.
steps.risk: This is the waiting-for-approval state only. Whichever you pick, I fit the running, paused and finished states to it afterwards — so judge the layout, not the coverage.

variants.label: Nested
variants.summary: The three helpers sit inside the step as their own cards, visible before you approve instead of hidden behind the arrow. The same nesting the card already uses once a plan is running.
variants.measured: 20 words of my own copy, against 22 on the card today
variants.risk: The tallest by about 40%, and it stays tall — eight helpers means eight cards you cannot fold away.

variants.label: Rows
variants.summary: Nothing but the app's universal row: the step's sentence, what feeds it underneath, the count as a badge, the standard chevron. Invents nothing at all.
variants.measured: 20 words of my own copy, against 22 on the card today
variants.risk: The fan-out is only a number until you click. The least different from what you are looking at today.

variants.label: Bar
variants.summary: The same rows, under a segmented bar whose widths are the plan's shape — three at once, then one, then one. The bar becomes the progress bar once the plan runs.
variants.measured: 20 words of my own copy, against 22 on the card today
variants.risk: The bar says the shape but not who does what. On pale themes it is a thin outline that could read as a divider.
